messages:
siva: ran a few nsys traces against the quantized 8-bit runner, mid-size batches (~6-10). seeing a weird kernel swap at ~200ms into requests, matmul kernel changes from matmul_fp16_opt to matmul_generic and latency jumps.
maria: that's odd — is it input-shape/pad related or a dynamic kernel-selection fallback? can you share the timeline snippet? :mag:
siva: pasted timeline ->
```
KernelTimeline:
  0-200ms: matmul_fp16_opt (avg 1.8ms)
  200-240ms: matmul_generic (avg 4.9ms)
  240-500ms: matmul_fp16_opt
```
Also seeing repeated CUPTI warnings in the nsys logs: `CUPTI error cuptiActivityEnable: CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_CMD_QUEUE` and some `metric collection disabled` warnings.
aj: those CUPTI warnings smell like a mismatch between nsys/CUPTI and the driver. which nsys + driver versions? and is this on dedicated or local devbox?
siva: nsys 2023.10.0 in container, driver 535.54.03 on host, CUDA 12.2. Repro on dedicated prod pool (container with seccomp profile). traces run via `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cupti --sample=cpu`.
ryan: seccomp + container can block CUPTI attaching to contexts. we saw attach failures before — nsys attaches to the process and uses CUPTI; if container blocks ptrace or necessary syscalls metrics silently degrade and you get weird kernel names. the kernel selector in the runtime falls back when metrics missing.
maria: that explains the fallback. but why only mid-run? should be deterministic per shape.
aj: batching heuristic uses recent kernel cost samples to pick variant. if CUPTI metrics are intermittently missing (attach fails for that request), estimator has stale/noisy data -> picks generic kernel until it regains confidence. leads to mid-stream jitter.
siva: confirmed by correlating timeline with nsys attach logs — there are windows where `cuptiActivityEnable` fails (permission denied) and our runtime switches kernel in the next batch.
ci-bot: automated test failing: throughput_regression_test quant-8b on dedicated pool dropped 12% after driver upgrade (job id: infra/throughput/4512).
ryan: noted on regression. possible remediation paths:
- ensure CUPTI attach succeeds in container (relax seccomp / give CAP_SYS_ADMIN / allow ptrace)
- pin a compatible nsys/CUPTI that tolerates driver 535.54.03 (we have a working combo with nsys 2024.1 + driver 535.86 on staging)
- add conservative kernel-selection fallback when metrics are missing (prefer old variant until >N successful samples)
maria: quick workaround: set env `RW_INFER_KERNEL_FORCE=matmul_fp16_opt` for the failing fleet to buy time. also add logging to kernel selector to mark 'metrics stale' state.
aj: i can add a small patch to runtime: only consider a variant switch if we have >=3 recent successful metric samples and relative improvement >8%. default to sticky variant otherwise.
siva: putting repro steps in thread: 1) run container with seccomp -> replicate nsys attach failures 2) run short-batch workload (batch size 8) with quantized model 3) observe kernel flip and 10-15% latency bump 4) repeat with CAP_SYS_ADMIN in container -> no flips.
ryan: action items:
- aj -> PR for selector safety net (ETA EOD)
- infra -> test allowing CUPTI attach in a canary pool (open ticket)
- release -> temporary env override for fleet (RW_INFER_KERNEL_FORCE)
- siva -> upload trimmed nsys traces + nsys log (please redact keys)
maria: small note: we should also check driver changelogs for scheduler changes around 535.x — there were some kernel naming / kernel cache invalidation fixes earlier that could influence heuristic stability.
siva: uploaded nsys ZIP to the trace bucket at s3://redwood-traces/1768523147-nsys.zip and added link to the infra ticket. I'll try with nsys 2024.1 in a side run and post results.
ryan: thanks — good triage. if anyone hits this in-prod, enable the env override and we can roll the selector patch quickly. :thumbsup:
